newsitem.title: USA: ConEd boosts NYC power output after fire.
newsitem.headline: ConEd boosts NYC power output after fire.

text.p: Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc (ConEd) said late Wednesday it was boosting power generation at its New York City facilities to compensate for restrictions on its system after a fire at a substation just north of the city.
Most of ConEd's New York City power plants burn fuel oil and/or natural gas.

A fire early today at the Sprain Brook power substation near Yonkers, N.Y. reduced power supplies from Canada and northern New York state to New York City, and led to a major power drop in southern New York, including Westchester County and Long Island.
"The fire is still smoldering. We expect it to be out shortly," ConEd spokesman Michael Spall said.
The fire inside one of three transformers in the substation shut six high-voltage transmission lines.
"We are going to look at the piece of equipment. We'll do a thorough investigation," Spall said, adding the substation was still in partial operation despite the fire.
The utility re-routed some transmission flows around the damaged substation to ensure power deliveries and stability to the regional grid, Spall said.

Long Island Lighting Co and Public Service Electric and Gas Co in New Jersey have been sending 950 megawatt (MW) of electricity to assist ConEd because of the curtailed flow of power to the city from upstate New York.
Spall said the city could import up to 5,000 MW of electricity. Power demand in the city peaked Wednesday at 7,276 MW.
About 1,500 MW of power to the city today came from nuclear generation, he added.
ConEd was still unclear how long it would take to repair the Sprain Brook substation or how long the north-south transmission limits would likely last, Spall said.
